title: Unbounded left derivability from a bounded-above resolving class
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive right exact functor, where right exact means preserving finite colimits. Let $\mathcal P\subseteq\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal A)$ contain $0$, be closed under finite direct sums, and have every object of $\mathcal A$ as an epimorphic image of an object of $\mathcal P$. Assume that $F(P^\bullet)$ is acyclic for every bounded above acyclic cochain complex $P^\bullet$ whose terms belong to $\mathcal P$. Assume also that both categories admit colimits of diagrams indexed by $\mathbf N$ with its usual order [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], these sequential colimits preserve short exact sequences of diagrams, and $F$ commutes with them. Then the left derived functor of $Q_{\mathcal B}\circ K(F):K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ is defined at every object in the sense of Situation 05S8 and Definition 05S9 [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]; here $K(F)$ applies $F$ termwise to complexes and homotopy classes of chain maps, and $Q_{\mathcal B}:K(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal B)$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms.

proof.text: Replace $\mathcal P$ by its isomorphism closure $\overline{\mathcal P}$. It contains every zero object, is closed under finite biproducts, and still covers every object by epimorphisms. The acyclicity hypothesis remains true: choose termwise isomorphisms from objects of $\mathcal P$ to the terms of an acyclic $\overline{\mathcal P}$-complex and conjugate its differentials. This gives an isomorphic acyclic $\mathcal P$-complex with the same upper bound, and applying $F$ gives an isomorphism of complexes. Thus work with $\overline{\mathcal P}$ throughout without adding a hypothesis to the item.

source.place: Tag 0794, hypothesis (1); isomorphism-closure convention needed for applying Tag 06XX as stated in the existing node.

proof.text: If $s:E\to E'$ is a quasi-isomorphism between bounded above $\overline{\mathcal P}$-complexes, its cone is acyclic by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]. Its terms are $E'^i\oplus E^{i+1}$, hence belong to $\overline{\mathcal P}$, and it is bounded above. The hypothesis makes $F(C(s))$ acyclic. Additivity identifies its differential matrix with the cone differential of $F(s)$, including the minus sign on the shifted summand. The same cone criterion in $\mathcal B$ makes $F(s)$ a quasi-isomorphism. This supplies precisely the preservation hypothesis of [lem-trf-bounded-stage-roof-comparison].

For any complex $K$, apply [lem-sfb-subcategory-truncation-resolution-system] to $\overline{\mathcal P}$. It gives bounded above $E_n$, strict compatible quasi-isomorphisms $E_n\to T_n=\tau_{\le n}K$, and transition maps. Form the termwise sequential colimit $E=\varinjlim E_n$ and its induced map $a:E\to K$. Exactness of sequential colimits in $\mathcal A$ and [src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits] identify $H^i(E)$ with $\varinjlim H^i(E_n)$. The explicit good truncation has $H^i(T_n)=H^i(K)$ for $i\le n$ and zero for $i>n$ (kernel/image at the cutoff gives the same quotient). The transition maps act as the identity on $H^i(K)$ once $n\ge\max(1,i)$. The colimit of this eventually constant system is $H^i(K)$, with comparison $H^i(a)$: a compatible cocone is uniquely determined on that constant tail. Hence $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

Let $\mathcal R$ be the class of complexes $X$ admitting a presentation $X=\varinjlim E_n$ by bounded above $\overline{\mathcal P}$-complexes with structure maps $e_n:E_n\to X$, such that $H^j(E_n)=0$ for $j>n$ and $H^j(e_n)$ is an isomorphism for $j\le n$. Isomorphic presentations are allowed. Step 3 supplies a quasi-isomorphism from an object of $\mathcal R$ to every $K$. Indeed its stages have the asserted vanishing because they resolve $T_n$; for $j\le n$ the equation $a e_n=(T_n\to K)(E_n\to T_n)$ and the isomorphism $H^j(a)$ show that $H^j(e_n)$ is an isomorphism. This uses no functorial choice of the towers and no additional bound on their terms.

source.place: Tag 0794, class of colimit resolutions used in the claim.

proof.text: Take a quasi-isomorphism $\alpha:X\to Y$ between objects of $\mathcal R$, and choose witnessing towers $E_n,G_n$. Step 2 verifies the preservation assumption of [lem-trf-bounded-stage-roof-comparison]; the augmentations satisfy all its other assumptions by the definition of $\mathcal R$. For each $i$ the lemma gives isomorphisms $\theta_n^i:H^i(F(E_n))\to H^i(F(G_n))$ commuting with the transition maps, and satisfying $H^i(F(g_n))\theta_n^i=H^i(F(\alpha))H^i(F(e_n))$. In particular the comparison is compatible with the actual map $F(\alpha)$ even though $\alpha$ need not be induced by a map of towers.

source.place: Tag 0794, proof of the claim; bounded roofs and compatibility as n varies.

proof.text: Since $F$ preserves sequential colimits, $F(X)=\varinjlim F(E_n)$ and $F(Y)=\varinjlim F(G_n)$, compatibly with their structure maps. Exact sequential colimits in $\mathcal B$ and [src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits] identify their cohomology with the colimits of the stage cohomology. The transition equation in step 5 makes $\theta_n^i$ a natural isomorphism of sequential diagrams, with natural inverse $(\theta_n^i)^{-1}$. The colimit universal property sends these inverse families to inverse maps. The second equation in step 5 identifies that colimit map with $H^i(F(\alpha))$, by its composites with every colimit leg. Thus $F(\alpha)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0794, final paragraph of the proof, using hypotheses (4) and (5).

proof.text: Use $C=K(\mathcal A)$, its quasi-isomorphisms $W$, and $H=D(\mathcal B)$ in [lem-pur-resolving-class-essential-constancy]. The required right calculus of fractions and two-out-of-three hold by [lem-pur-quasi-isos-saturated-triangulated]. Step 4 supplies $W$-arrows from $\mathcal R$ to every object, and steps 5–6 show that $Q_{\mathcal B}K(F)$ inverts every $W$-arrow between objects of $\mathcal R$. Thus every denominator diagram $W/K\to D(\mathcal B)$ is essentially constant. The same quasi-isomorphism-system node gives the triangulated localization setup; additivity of $F$ preserves the shift and cone matrices displayed in step 2, so $K(F)$ is exact, and $Q_{\mathcal B}$ is exact. These are the assumptions of Situation 05S8. By the definition in [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], the essential constancy just proved says that the left derived functor is defined at every object, as required.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q104-a4fd730eb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks derived.tex Tag 0794 (proposition-left-derived-exists) in full. The item matches hypotheses (1)-(5) and the 05S9 everywhere-defined conclusion, with nothing weakened. Its seven steps are correct. Step 1 (isomorphism closure, elementary) is needed for the 06XX node's hypotheses. Step 2 is the cone criterion via lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic, with F(C(s))=C(F(s)). Step 3 builds the 06XX tower and identifies cohomology through src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits plus the eventually constant good-truncation system. Step 4 defines the class R by the identity a·ι_n=(T_n→K)e_n. Step 6 is the colimit of the natural isomorphism θ, identified with H^i(F(α)) through the colimit legs. Step 7 uses lem-pur-resolving-class-essential-constancy, lem-pur-quasi-isos-saturated-triangulated and def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization; all their hypotheses are met. The new node lem-trf-bounded-stage-roof-comparison is true: φ_n is the unique D-morphism with g_nφ_n=αe_n, using G_n≅τ≤nY and E_n∈D^{≤n}. A P̄-resolved roof gives θ_n as an isomorphism, and F preserves homotopies, which gives the square. The transition equation follows by uniqueness in D^{≤n+1}. I tested it on X=Y=0, α=id, negative i, and stages with terms above n. It is statement-only and self-contained. It fills the source's 'exact same argument' compatibility gap, so it is not a restatement of the item (D1). A duplicate search over 0794, 05T7, 06XN, 06XX and the left-derived existence nodes found no duplicate of the helper or of the item. Stacks' α: Q→P against its diagrams is a harmless notational correction. I accept the five generic homological-algebra tool_uses. No SGA source is used. No fixes.
